title: State
description: A semantically meaningful situation the application can be in. The most important object in the model: a state owns what can be perceived, what can be done, and - separately from both - what is being OFFERED but was never taken (affordances[]).

description.description: Human/LLM readable summary, e.g. 'Checkout page for an authenticated user with items in cart'.

elements.description: Interactive/perceivable elements present in this state.

behaviors.description: Behaviours available while on this surface. Inverse view of transitions[].from_state; derive it or omit it.

affordances.description: What this surface offers that the model has not performed. Everywhere else in the document, absence means 'not known'; this array is the one place the model states a positive reading of something it did not do.

outgoing_transitions.description: Optional denormalised index. Derived from transitions[].from_state; keep it consistent or omit it.

apis.description: APIs the application calls while in this state (initial data loads).

detection.description: How a test proves it is in this state. Should pin route + the discriminating elements/values from identity.dimensions.

stateIdentity.description: The identity of the state. A URL is an identity SIGNAL, not the identity: /checkout with an empty cart and /checkout with a coupon applied are two states. Two states must differ in at least one of page_type / variant / dimensions.

route.description: URL path or path pattern, e.g. /checkout or /product/:slug. Absent for states that are not URL addressable (modals, overlays).

page_type.description: Coarse semantic page kind: home, product_detail, cart, checkout, order_confirmation, login, 404.

variant.description: Named variant of the same page_type: authenticated, anonymous, admin, mobile, ab_test_b. A variant names a surface and not a role: authenticated and anonymous are authentication states, mobile a presentation and ab_test_b an experiment, and none of the five says who is looking at the page. Roles are declared in application.actors[], and where a declaration names this variant the surface is exercised as that actor.

dimensions.description: Discriminating facts that separate sibling states sharing route+page_type+variant. Keep it small and semantic: {cart: non_empty, coupon: applied}.

route_params.description: Concrete parameter values seen in evidence, e.g. {slug: 'blue-shirt'}.

query.description: Query string keys that are identity-relevant.

title.description: Observed document title, as a weak identity signal.

affordance.description: Something this surface OFFERS that the model did not take. An affordance is a claim about the APPLICATION, not a statement about our coverage: the element is present, it reads as doing this, and no committed step has contradicted it. Because it is a claim it must be falsifiable - the element has to be declared in this same state's elements[] (P13), and a committed realization step on that element RETIRES the affordance instead of confirming it, because the interaction then belongs in behavior.realization[] where its effects are recorded.

element.description: The element in THIS state that offers the behaviour.

expected_behavior.description: The behaviour the element appears to offer, named in the same register as behavior.name - a verb phrase such as reset_password, list_projects, sign_out.
